annotations.title: Find similar homes in another city

description:
Homes like one listing, in another city, side by side with it.

    Use when the user likes a home and asks what something similar costs, or
    looks like, elsewhere ("homes like #2 in Lisbon"). Returns the listing and
    up to 2 matches in `city`, each with asking price, price per m², stated
    features, environment readings (quiet, clean air, leafy, coastal, flood /
    wildfire / seismic / ground-motion screening), walk and drive minutes, and
    the region's climate.

    Matches have the same bedrooms and a living area within 15%, and are
    picked on features and environment — never on price — so the price
    difference is a finding, not how they were chosen. Relay it as asking
    prices, never as a saving, a valuation or a "city premium". A feature
    marked "not_stated" means the listing doesn't say, not that the home lacks
    it; an environment value "unknown" means there is no reading. When
    `matches` is empty, say no documented match was found; do not loosen it.

    With `compare_with` (a second listing id) instead of `city`, no search
    runs: the two listings come back side by side on the same rows — e.g.
    the top home of each city in a comparison, feature by feature.

    Args:
        listing_id: Source-prefixed id of a listing already shown (e.g.
            `remax:12345`). Do not invent one.
        city: The other city to search in, e.g. "Lisboa".
        compare_with: A second listing id already shown, to compare the two.
        lang: ISO 639-1 code (en/pt/es/fr/de/nl/ru).

    Returns:
        JSON: seed and matches[] with price, eur_per_m2, features, environment
        {axis: {state, value, unit}}, minutes, climate, and a `card` with the
        listing link; or a not-found / same-city message.
name: find_similar_elsewhere
title: Find similar homes in another city
